title: Unit – 4 : Session – 8 : SLO – 1  |  AVL Tree — Rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL)
sections: I. LL and RR Rotations
In an AVL tree, LL rotation is performed when a node becomes unbalanced due to insertion in the LEFT subtree of its LEFT child.
LL Rotation is a type of SINGLE (right) rotation used to balance an AVL tree.
After an LL rotation, the height difference between the left and right subtrees of the previously unbalanced node becomes at most 1.
In an LL rotation, the left child of the unbalanced node becomes the new ROOT of the subtree.
The time complexity of an LL rotation operation in an AVL tree is O(1).
RR rotation is used in an AVL tree when a node becomes unbalanced due to insertion in the RIGHT subtree of its RIGHT child.
RR rotation is a type of SINGLE (left) rotation in AVL trees.
In RR rotation, the right child of the unbalanced node becomes the new ROOT of the subtree.
After an RR rotation, the height difference between the left and right subtrees of the previously unbalanced node becomes at most 1.
The time complexity of an RR rotation operation in an AVL tree is O(1).
II. LR and RL Rotations
In an AVL tree, LR rotation is performed when the left child of a node is RIGHT heavy.
LR rotation is a combination of LEFT (RR) rotation followed by RIGHT (LL) rotation.
To fix an imbalance at a node caused by insertion in the right subtree of its left child, we perform an LR rotation.
After an LR rotation, the node that was inserted becomes the ROOT of the subtree.
In LR rotation, the imbalance occurs at node A, and its left child B has a right child C; the first step is a LEFT (RR) rotation on node B.
RL rotation is required when a node becomes unbalanced due to insertion in the LEFT subtree of its RIGHT child.
RL rotation is a combination of two rotations: first a RIGHT (LL) rotation on the right child, followed by a LEFT (RR) rotation on the unbalanced node.
RL rotation is a type of DOUBLE rotation in AVL trees.
In RL rotation, the node that becomes the new root of the subtree is the LEFT child of the right child of the unbalanced node.
The main goal of performing an RL rotation is to restore the BALANCE (height-balance) property of the AVL tree.
